proof: The Bezier derivative ratio is a convex combination of control differences dy/dx weighted by positive Bernstein derivative dx terms. Therefore abs(dy/dx) <=max(0,16/120,2/58)=2/15. Two Y-translated graphs with Lipschitz bound M have minimum distance >=w/sqrt(1+M²): minimize dx²+(w-M*abs(dx))², with the region M*abs(dx)>=w giving no smaller bound.
scope: Only paired long XY walls, excluding other cuts, caps, arch and intersections; exact thickness audit still required.
